question: Which of the following organisations was given statutory power in 1992?
solution:
The correct answer is __**SEBI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was given statutory powers on **30 January 1992** through the SEBI Act, 1992.
 
• SEBI was initially established as a non-statutory body in **1988** and later got statutory powers to regulate the securities market in India.
 
• The primary objective of SEBI is to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote and regulate the securities market.
 
• SEBI's functions include regulating stock exchanges and other securities markets, registering and regulating the working of intermediaries, and prohibiting fraudulent and unfair trade practices.
 
• SEBI has the authority to conduct inspections, audits, and investigations to ensure compliance with regulations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of SEBI:**

 
 
• Regulating the business in stock exchanges and other securities markets.
 
• Registering and regulating the working of various intermediaries like brokers, merchant bankers, and portfolio managers.
 
• Prohibiting insider trading and regulating substantial acquisition of shares and takeovers of companies.
 
• Promoting and regulating self-regulatory organizations.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of SEBI:**
 
 
• To protect the interests of investors in securities.
 
• To promote the development of and to regulate the securities market.
 
• To ensure fair practices in the securities market and protect investors from fraudulent activities.
 
 
 
• **Key Functions of SEBI:**
 
 
• Regulatory functions such as imposing penalties and taking actions against market violations.
 
• Developmental functions aimed at promoting and improving the securities market.
 
• Investor protection functions including educating and informing investors about their rights and market conditions.
 
 
 
• **SEBI's Structure:**
 
 
• SEBI consists of a Chairman appointed by the Government of India, two members from the Ministry of Finance, one member from the Reserve Bank of India, and five other members out of which at least three shall be whole-time members.
 
• SEBI's headquarters is located in Mumbai, and it has regional offices in New Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, and Ahmedabad.
